html:
Bujumbura, the largest city of Burundi, began as Usumbura, a German military post founded in 1889 on the northeast shore of Lake Tanganyika.

Under Belgian rule it was the capital of all of Ruanda-Urundi, and its lake port linked the region to Kigoma and the railway to the coast. It had a mixed population of Africans from many places, Swahili traders, Asians and Europeans.

It became the capital of Burundi at independence and took its present name. It was fought over in the civil war, when its Hutu quarters were cleared by the army. In 2019 the government made Gitega, the old royal centre, the political capital, but Bujumbura is still the economic heart of the country.
sum: Bujumbura, the largest city of Burundi, began as Usumbura, a German military post founded in 1889 on the northeast shore of Lake Tanganyika.
